A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 24-page work, Action-Guided Attention for Video Action Anticipation, including Appendices A–D. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original AGA experiments on EPIC-Kitchens-100, EPIC-Kitchens-55 and EGTEA Gaze+. Appendices B–C include additional experiments and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, robustness experiments and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Action-prediction queries and keys, EMA query construction, adaptive gating, and forward/backward analysis procedures in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use EPIC-Kitchens-100, EPIC-Kitchens-55 and EGTEA Gaze+ for the same action-anticipation tasks and test scenarios, including appendix experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. S-GEAR remains the same Table 1 comparator; revising its scores does not change the baseline set.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–B retain the same data splits, preprocessing, metrics, anticipation intervals, training settings and testing procedures.

E4.justification: Component ablations, EMA and queue-size sweeps, computational-cost comparisons, error-propagation tests, guidance-signal comparisons and qualitative case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Run descriptions and statistical reporting are identical. Neither version provides confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: In Table 1, S-GEAR's EK100 overall-class verb MT5R changes from 32.0 to 25.9, while noun MT5R changes from 25.9 to 32.0. AGA's unchanged 30.8 consequently becomes the highest listed verb score. All other numerical and qualitative results, including appendix results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3's formal task definition, attention and gating equations, and backward-analysis optimization are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about action-guided attention, generalization, adaptive gating and interpretability.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization, action dependencies and gating behavior are unchanged, as are Appendix C's discussions of failures involving occlusion, ambiguous objects and insufficient visual evidence.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information and code/data access instructions in Sections 4.1 and 6 and Appendices A–B are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 2's positioning against previous anticipation methods are identical. The S-GEAR score revision does not alter the accompanying research-positioning discussion.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 2 March 2026, to v2, dated 9 May 2026. Manuscript prose, terminology and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 removes bold emphasis from S-GEAR's former 32.0 verb score and bolds AGA's unchanged 30.8. Table structures, captions, figures and their placement remain unchanged, including throughout the appendices.

improvement.justification: The only substantive revision swaps two cited S-GEAR scores and updates the highlighted winner in Table 1. Neither PDF explains or independently substantiates which assignment is correct, so the local evidence cannot establish whether this improves reporting accuracy. The method, experiments, discussion and appendices otherwise remain unchanged.
